comment: Incident replay registry (P1.4). Every entry names a real, dated failure from the bench/launch era, its root cause, its fix, and the permanent regression tests that lock it. tests/test_incident_replay.py validates this registry's integrity AND replays each incident class against the live tree. Adding an incident without regression tests fails the suite.

incidents.title: Permission-pattern probing caused tool denials and cost blowup in bench arms
incidents.source: workbench-vnext / ai-workbench-rc bench era, 2026-10 (run_arm.py ALLOWED evolution; r3 note '9 denials from cmd/cd retries'; first controlled A/B measured 2.33x baseline cost partly from permission trial-and-error)
incidents.root_cause: Bench arms ran with asymmetric/incomplete allowedTools (Bash entries without PowerShell counterparts on Windows), so agents burned turns probing which shell spelling was permitted; every denial was a paid turn. The product-side risk twin: an over-broad allowlist would have 'fixed' it by disabling the permission model.
incidents.fix: Paired Bash(x:*)/PowerShell(x:*) prefixes limited to what a bugfix session legitimately needs; no bare wildcards; SDK bench runner uses bypassPermissions (bench-only, documented); the installed product settings carry NO permissions key (Claude Code defaults stay in force).
incidents.reproduce: Give one arm Bash(python:*) but not PowerShell(python:*) on Windows; count permission denials in the transcript.

incidents.title: verify.py resolved its workspace from __file__ and checked the wrong directory
incidents.root_cause: A verify script that anchors on __file__ checks the repo/task directory, not the agent's workspace copy — it can PASS while the agent did nothing, or FAIL while the agent succeeded. Companion failure: the agent (with write access beyond the workspace) could rewrite its own examiner.
incidents.fix: All task verify scripts resolve the workspace from Path.cwd() (the driver runs them with cwd=workspace) and carry the marker protocol (VERIFY PASS / VERIFY FAIL: <reason>) so a crash (traceback, no marker) is never confused with a real verification failure. run_sdk_arm.py hashes the verify script pre/post agent run; any modification voids the result (verify_tampered).
incidents.reproduce: Point a verify script at Path(__file__).parent and run it against a modified workspace: it reports on the pristine task dir instead.

incidents.title: __pycache__ artifacts polluted provenance/drift scans
incidents.root_cause: Interpreter-generated __pycache__ directories appear and disappear with runtime, not with human edits; scanning them makes caches indistinguishable from real unauthorized changes (fake drift) and can hide real ones in the noise.
incidents.fix: check_hygiene.py SKIP_DIRS excludes __pycache__ (and .pytest_cache etc.); behavioral contracts prove a planted cache file with forbidden content is ignored while the same content in a real source file is caught.
incidents.reproduce: Drop a .pyc-adjacent text file containing a personal path into __pycache__/ and watch a naive scanner report drift; then put the same string into a real .py and watch it pass if the scanner over-skips.

incidents.title: Builder-machine user paths risked leaking into the publish set
incidents.source: launch sprint era, 2026-10 (F:\Claude... builder paths; relay tooling had to be gitignored)
incidents.root_cause: Docs and configs generated on the builder machine naturally contain absolute user paths; publishing them leaks personal directory structure. The inverse risk: a paranoid pattern false-positiving on documentation placeholders makes the gate useless.
incidents.fix: check_hygiene.py scans exactly the publishable set (git ls-files, so local evidence like bench results stays out) for drive/project/user-profile/secret shapes, with a lookahead that exempts placeholders like C:\Users\...\project; self-reference allowlist for the checkers themselves; the release archive (zipapp) contents are scanned too.
incidents.reproduce: echo 'C:\Users\someone\project' into a tracked file and run tools/check_hygiene.py.
